title: Looking good but rotten in the old fashioned ‘Microsoft’ way
body:
Most features from the great Wunderlist app are, as a years dedicated user,good.
But then, your user has to be signed in million times per week (not to be confused with the stable Wunderlist login),and then it fails,cause Microsoft 🤷🏼‍♀️ And why would you be able to work on your list locally on your phone and afterwards solve the user login?! Na.

You had some (by some I mean, about 6) light weight images pinned here and there to a list item? Na, after a very small quota Microsoft can’t handle all your rubbish. You need to download the entire backup from Wunderlist. Who knows, you will probably pay for it soon to be upgraded.

I was very sad but hopeful, when Wunderlist was acquired bu Microsoft. What was I expecting...

title: Mediocre replacement for Wunderlist
body:
Microsoft To Do wanted to be a good alternative for Wunderlist. Unfortunately, all the good features, simplicity and stability of Wunderlist were thrown away in favor of less intuitive and less stable app.

NOTE: For simple “To do” tasks, this app is fine. Once you start using it heavily like I do - that’s were the things go sideways.

title: Chikko
body:
Update: Microsoft, you got approximately 3 months till Sep 2019 to outdo yourselves - as apple's overhauled native reminders app seems to be everything we need from a reminders app, and more.

The only reason I'm still using the app is the hope i still have due to the fact that it came from the creators of Wunderlist. I was real patient at first, and constantly waited to watch it grow with every update, but the small bug fixes which are being released every 2 weeks just won't cut it: The app misses tons of capabilities which were already an integral part of Wunderlist, and tons of other features which would have made the app relevant for iOS 12 (such as Siri shortcuts). I'm truly disappointed from Microsoft for not allowing more frequent and meaningful updates for this app.
